notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood for core inference. Started on hosted API to validate accuracy and latency for chat-support and doc search; two-week POC completed with hosted infra. POC notes: p95 generation latency ~180ms EU, throughput steady at 2k requests/day with peaks to 4k. Embedding vectors (1536-d) match quality targets; reranking model reduces hit-rate false positives by ~12% vs baseline. Customer pain: unpredictable per-token bills during spikes -> wants predictable monthly cost. Preference: move to Dedicated for cost predictability and VPC/network controls but keep hosted for overflow during ramp.

Pricing negotiation specifics (summarized):
- Customer asked for a 12-month committed plan. Proposal options discussed:
  * Option A (conservative): Commit to 75 GPU-hours/day (baseline), ramping 3-month linear to 150 GPU-hours/day by month 4. Monthly billing = committed units at discounted rate; overage billed at 1.5x committed unit price.
  * Option B (aggressive): Commit to 150 GPU-hours/day with 20% discount and an included 2x burst pool for traffic spikes (burst available up to 24 hours per month). Overage beyond burst billed at 1.25x committed price.
  * Option C (phased ramp): 6-month initial commit at 50 GPU-hours/day with formal ramp schedule and a quarterly re-evaluation clause; burst capacity as pay-as-you-go (higher per-unit price).
- Burst: Customer needs guaranteed short-term burst (2-3x baseline) for product releases. They requested automatic burst for 30 minutes on sudden traffic surges and the ability to pre-schedule larger bursts for planned campaigns.
- Overage mechanics: Customer insisted on caps and notifications. Proposed guardrails: soft-limit alerts at 80% of commit, hard-limit if enabled, and negotiated overage caps (limit to 25% of committed spend unless pre-approved).
- Ramp schedule: Customer expects onboarding incremental scale: start with core 3 services (support chat, search, summarization) then enable embeddings batch jobs in month 2. Proposed 3-phase rollout (canary -> regional ramp -> full). Billing ramp credits offered if missed SLA during ramp.
- Legal/security asks: EU data residency clause in SOW, SOC2 plus audit log retention 2 years, KMS integration with customer key, SSO/SAML for console access. They require indemnity language for data leakage and a right-to-audit window.

Internal signals/quotes: "We need predictable unit economics — spikes wreck our margins" (CTO). "If we can lock a committed pool and a safe burst policy, we'll migrate production flows" (Head of Platform). Procurement pushing for a 6-12 month ramp and a clear overage cap.

Open items for Redwood sales: finalize concrete committed-unit pricing (per GPU-hour), confirm burst pricing and SLA during burst, provide an EU-residency SOW addendum and a sample billing ramp schedule. Also need a worked example monthly forecast with expected overage scenarios (conservative, expected, worst-case).
